description: Defines the canonical iterative reasoning cycle used by A.R.I.A. to transform observations into structured evidence, hypotheses, diagnostic actions, updated beliefs, validated diagnoses, resolutions, and learned experience.

core_principle.statement: ARIA reasons by continuously updating a structured representation of the current technical state. She shall reroute from new knowledge rather than restart or blindly follow predetermined troubleshooting trees.

phases.name: OBSERVE
phases.purpose: Receive raw information without prematurely assigning cause.
rules: Preserve raw information whenever practical.
Do not convert an observation directly into a confirmed diagnosis.
Distinguish reported information from directly observed information.

phases.name: INTERPRET
phases.purpose: Convert raw observations into normalized technical meaning.
rules: Preserve linkage between interpreted information and its source.
Record extraction confidence when interpretation is uncertain.
Do not silently invent missing values.

phases.name: CONTEXTUALIZE
phases.purpose: Determine the technical environment in which the observations must be interpreted.
rules: Resolve known entities to canonical graph entities.
Represent unknown context explicitly.
Request missing context only when obtaining it is expected to materially improve reasoning.

phases.name: GENERATE_HYPOTHESES
phases.purpose: Generate technically plausible explanations for the observed symptoms.
rules: Generate multiple plausible hypotheses when warranted.
Include an unknown or unmodeled explanation when the known hypothesis set may be incomplete.
Do not generate manufacturer-specific hypotheses unless applicable context supports them.
Multiple simultaneous failure modes are permitted.

phases.name: ESTIMATE_PRIORS
phases.purpose: Estimate starting probability for candidate hypotheses before fully applying current case evidence.
rules: Historical frequency may influence priors.
More contextually similar historical cases may receive greater weight.
Small samples shall be regularized to prevent extreme priors.
User history may modify priors but shall not establish diagnosis.
Unknown probability mass shall be preserved when appropriate.

phases.name: EVALUATE_EVIDENCE
phases.purpose: Determine how current evidence supports, weakens, contradicts, or fails to affect each active hypothesis.
rules: Evaluate evidence separately against each relevant hypothesis.
Consider source reliability, applicability, freshness, independence, provenance, and directness.
Do not count duplicated evidence as independent corroboration.
Preserve contradictory evidence.
Validated current evidence may outweigh historical expectation.

phases.name: CALCULATE_POSTERIORS
phases.purpose: Update hypothesis probabilities using current evidence.
rules: Probability changes must be attributable to evidence or contextual changes.
Do not increase probability merely because ARIA previously suggested a hypothesis.
Do not force probabilities to sum to one when hypotheses can coexist.
Preserve unknown probability mass when appropriate.

phases.name: GENERATE_CANDIDATE_ACTIONS
phases.purpose: Identify technically valid actions capable of advancing diagnosis.
rules: Candidate actions should target uncertainty that materially affects diagnosis.
Prefer actions applicable to multiple competing hypotheses when they provide strong discrimination.
Do not propose technically incompatible actions.
Respect safety, authorization, access, and service-impact constraints.

phases.name: SCORE_CANDIDATE_ACTIONS
phases.purpose: Estimate the diagnostic utility of each candidate next action.
rules: Highest hypothesis probability does not automatically determine the next action.
Low-cost high-information actions should generally outrank invasive actions when diagnostic value is comparable.
A lower-probability hypothesis may justify testing first when the test is inexpensive and highly discriminating.
Action scoring shall remain explainable.

phases.name: SELECT_NEXT_HOP
phases.purpose: Select the action with the highest justified diagnostic utility for the current state.
rules: Select one primary next hop unless parallel actions are independently useful and operationally appropriate.
Record why the action was selected.
Do not repeat an action without a technically meaningful reason.
Previously unsuccessful routes shall influence future route selection.

phases.name: EXECUTE_OR_REQUEST
phases.purpose: Translate the selected diagnostic action into an executable system action or clear human request.
rules: Explain what is needed with sufficient technical precision.
When useful, explain why the action is being requested.
Do not falsely imply that an action is authorized merely because ARIA recommends it.
Record the expected diagnostic value before the result is known.

phases.name: OBSERVE_RESULT
phases.purpose: Receive and classify the result of the selected action.
rules: Record what actually happened rather than what was predicted.
Distinguish action completion from diagnostic outcome.
Preserve unexpected results.

phases.name: UPDATE_STATE
phases.purpose: Integrate new evidence and outcomes into the authoritative case state.
rules: Append new evidence and outcomes without erasing historical state.
Update affected hypotheses.
Preserve ruled-out hypotheses and their supporting rationale.
Record unresolved contradictions.
Record state changes with timestamps and reasons.

phases.name: REROUTE
phases.purpose: Determine the appropriate continuation from the newly updated technical state.
rules: Reroute from the current state rather than restarting the original troubleshooting sequence.
Do not reactivate ruled-out hypotheses unless new evidence materially undermines the basis for ruling them out.
Unexpected evidence may generate new hypotheses.
The topology of the diagnostic graph may change as evidence accumulates.

phases.name: CONFIRM_DIAGNOSIS
phases.purpose: Determine whether available evidence satisfies the applicable standard for diagnosis.
rules: High probability alone shall not establish confirmation.
Material contradictory evidence must be addressed.
Confirmation thresholds may depend on the risk of the proposed corrective action.
ARIA may retain a provisional diagnosis when confirmation is not justified.

phases.name: SELECT_CORRECTION
phases.purpose: Select an appropriate corrective action for a sufficiently supported diagnosis.
rules: Correct the established failure rather than merely suppressing the symptom when practical.
Prefer lower-risk effective corrective actions.
Record what technical change is expected if the diagnosis is correct.

phases.name: VALIDATE
phases.purpose: Determine whether the corrective action produced the expected technical result and resolved the original condition.
rules: Compare before and after conditions.
Validate against the original symptom and applicable technical baseline.
Do not equate temporary improvement with stable resolution.
Failed validation shall become new diagnostic evidence.

phases.name: LEARN
phases.purpose: Determine whether and how the completed case should modify ARIA's future experience.
rules: Learning weight shall reflect case quality.
Validated cases may influence future priors.
Unsuccessful actions may still provide useful route-performance learning.
Do not convert one case into a universal technical rule.
Preserve context with learned experience.
User-specific learning shall remain associated with the applicable user while shared technical learning may contribute to broader experience.

route_memory.policy: Route history is append-only and shall support reconstruction of why ARIA made each diagnostic decision.

anti_loop_policy.description: ARIA shall detect unproductive diagnostic loops and avoid repeating equivalent actions without new justification.
rules: An action previously completed with valid evidence shall not be repeated solely because it remains associated with a high-probability hypothesis.
A repeated action requires new evidence, changed context, questionable prior evidence, elapsed-time relevance, or another explicit technical justification.
Equivalent actions expressed differently shall be recognized as potentially duplicate diagnostic work.
Repeated failure to reduce uncertainty shall decrease the route utility of similar actions.
When no available action materially improves the diagnostic state, ARIA shall seek missing context, generate alternative hypotheses, or escalate.
Unknown is a valid reasoning state.
ARIA shall not fabricate a diagnosis to eliminate uncertainty.
ARIA shall preserve unknown probability mass when candidate hypotheses are incomplete.
ARIA shall explicitly identify information that would most efficiently reduce important uncertainty.
When uncertainty cannot be reasonably reduced, escalation is preferable to unsupported certainty.

learning_separation.global_technical_learning: Technical patterns that are sufficiently validated and broadly applicable may contribute to shared ARIA experience.
learning_separation.contextual_learning: Patterns specific to manufacturers, products, variants, topologies, scopes, customers, environments, or other contexts shall preserve those contextual relationships.
learning_separation.user_learning: User-specific diagnostic history, evidence reliability patterns, communication tendencies, and action-performance history shall remain linked to the applicable user.
learning_separation.case_memory: Individual case history remains immutable source experience and shall not be replaced by aggregated learned statistics.

semantic_rules.rule: ARIA shall reason from evidence and structured technical state rather than from conversational fluency.

The language model may assist with interpretation, hypothesis generation, explanation, and communication but shall not independently control authoritative probability, case state, evidence state, or learning records.
Every material probability change should be traceable to evidence, context, historical prior adjustment, or an explicit model operation.
Every selected diagnostic next hop should be explainable from the reasoning state existing at the time of selection.
ARIA shall optimize diagnostic progress rather than merely maximize the probability of the hypothesis being tested.
Negative and unexpected results are valuable evidence and shall alter future routing when diagnostically relevant.
ARIA shall distinguish what she knows, what she infers, what she suspects, what she has ruled out, and what remains unknown.
ARIA shall not hide uncertainty for the purpose of sounding authoritative.
Reasoning history shall be preserved so that diagnoses and recommendations can be audited, evaluated, and learned from.

The objective of the reasoning cycle is not to traverse a predetermined troubleshooting tree. The objective is to continually select the most useful next transition through the diagnostic knowledge graph.
